proposals.before: While Wuhuang held Yanmen, thirteen-year-old Siyuan, then in Dai, impressed Xianzu with his riding and archery; Xianzu stroked him and said, "Spirit like your father—you may wait on me."
proposals.after: While Wuhuang held Yanmen, Xiaocheng passed away; the Emperor was just thirteen and skilled at mounted archery; Xianzu saw him, stroked him, and said, "Spirit like your father—you may wait on me."
proposals.reason: 厭代 is a death euphemism for Xiaocheng, not the place name Dai.

proposals.before: When Wuhuang held Yanmen, Xiaocheng was in Dai, and the Emperor was just thirteen, skilled at mounted archery; Xianzu saw him, stroked him, and said, "Spirit like your father—you may attend at my side."
proposals.after: When Wuhuang held Yanmen, Xiaocheng passed away, and the Emperor was just thirteen, skilled at mounted archery; Xianzu saw him, stroked him, and said, "Spirit like your father—you may attend at my side."
proposals.reason: 厭代 means death, not that Xiaocheng was in Dai.

proposals.before: In Qianning 3 Liang armies pressed Yan and Yun; Zhu Xuan of Yan begged Wuhuang for aid.
proposals.after: In Qianning 3 Liang armies pressed Yan and Yun; Zhu Xuan of Yun begged Wuhuang for aid.
proposals.reason: 鄆帥朱瑄 is the Yun commander; Yan is one of the besieged prefectures, not Zhu Xuan's title.

proposals.before: In the third year of Qianning, Liang forces pressed Yan and Yun fiercely; Yan military commissioner Zhu Xuan begged Wuhuang for rescue.
proposals.after: In the third year of Qianning, Liang forces pressed Yan and Yun fiercely; Yun military commissioner Zhu Xuan begged Wuhuang for rescue.
proposals.reason: 鄆帥 means Yun's commander, not Yan's.

proposals.before: His great-great-grandmother, Lady Cui of the State of Wei, was posthumously given the temple name Empress Xiaogong Zhao.
proposals.after: His great-great-grandmother, Lady Cui of the State of Wei, was posthumously given the posthumous title Empress Xiaogong Zhao.
proposals.reason: 追諡 is a posthumous honorific, not a temple name.

proposals.before: Cornered, Xingqin bound his face and surrendered; Siyuan gave him wine, clapped his back, and said, "My boy, what a fighter!"
proposals.after: Cornered, Xingqin bound his hands behind his back and surrendered; Siyuan gave him wine, clapped his back, and said, "My boy, what a fighter!"
proposals.reason: 面縛 means binding the hands behind the back in surrender, not binding the face.

proposals.before: Xingqin was cornered, bound his face, and begged surrender; the Emperor poured wine for him to drink, patted his back, and said, "My boy, what a brave fellow!"
proposals.after: Xingqin was cornered, bound his hands behind his back, and begged surrender; the Emperor poured wine for him to drink, patted his back, and said, "My boy, what a brave fellow!"
proposals.reason: 面縛 is the surrender posture of having the hands bound behind the back, not a literal binding of the face.

proposals.before: In the fourth month Xiangzhou's Zhang Yun fled; he was then made Xiang prefectural governor.
proposals.after: In the fourth month Xiangzhou's Zhang Yun fled; the Emperor was then made Xiang prefectural governor.
proposals.reason: The Chinese subject of 乃以帝為相州刺史 is the Emperor (Siyuan), not Zhang Yun; the literal 'he' reverses the appointment.

proposals.before: In the fourth month of year 14 Khitan Anbajian besieged Youzhou; Zhou Dewei sent urgent word, and Zhuangzong asked his generals how to relieve it; they said the Khitan could not stay long and should be struck only after they withdrew for hunger."
proposals.after: In the fourth month of year 14 Khitan Anbajian besieged Youzhou; Zhou Dewei sent urgent word, and Zhuangzong asked his generals how to relieve it; they said the Khitan could not stay long and should be struck only after they withdrew for hunger.
proposals.reason: A stray closing quotation mark is appended after the paraphrase of the generals' advice, which is not presented as a closed quotation in this idiomatic sentence.

proposals.before: The Emperor said to the generals, "Enemy horse live on the saddle and need no camps; moreover they are many and we few—we should hold arrows in the mouth, clamp the horses' mouths, steal along streams and ravines, and strike them unprepared."
proposals.after: The Emperor said to the generals, "Enemy horse live on the saddle and need no camps; moreover they are many and we few—we should hold gags in the mouth, clamp the horses' mouths, steal along streams and ravines, and strike them unprepared."
proposals.reason: 銜枚 means soldiers holding wooden gags, not arrows; 箝馬 is clamping the horses' mouths.

proposals.before: That day the generals congratulated him; Cunxu handed wine to Siyuan and said, "Yesterday at Chaocheng many of you wanted to abandon Yan and make the river the border; only the deputy overall commander held the front and Chongtao schemed within—had I listened to Li Shaohong and his crowd, the cause would be dust."
proposals.after: That day the generals congratulated him; Cunxu handed wine to Siyuan and said, "Yesterday at Chaocheng many of you wanted to abandon Yun and make the river the border; only the deputy overall commander held the front and Chongtao schemed within—had I listened to Li Shaohong and his crowd, the cause would be dust."
proposals.reason: Chinese 棄鄆州 is Yun (鄆), not Yan; the idiomatic rendering invents the wrong prefecture.

proposals.before: That day the generals offered congratulations; Zhuangzong passed wine to the Emperor, saying, "Yesterday I was at Chaocheng; many of you urged me to abandon Yanzhou and take the river as boundary; relying on the deputy overall commander to repel insult in front and Chongtao to scheme within, if I had believed Li Shaohong and his sort, the great affair would already have been swept away."
proposals.after: That day the generals offered congratulations; Zhuangzong passed wine to the Emperor, saying, "Yesterday I was at Chaocheng; many of you urged me to abandon Yunzhou and take the river as boundary; relying on the deputy overall commander to repel insult in front and Chongtao to scheme within, if I had believed Li Shaohong and his sort, the great affair would already have been swept away."
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou (兗/燕); the literal line mismatches the source toponym.

proposals.before: In the sixth month he became Grand Preceptor, took Bian as military commissioner, and replaced Li Cun'an as Han and non-Han overall commander.
proposals.after: In the sixth month he became Grand Commandant, took Bian as military commissioner, and replaced Li Cunshen as Han and non-Han overall commander.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Preceptor (太傅); 李存審 is the same Li Cunshen named earlier, not Li Cun'an.

proposals.before: Sixth month: he was promoted to Grand Preceptor, transferred to hold Bianzhou, replacing Li Cun'an as Han and non-Han overall commander.
proposals.after: Sixth month: he was promoted to Grand Commandant, transferred to hold Bianzhou, replacing Li Cunshen as Han and non-Han overall commander.
proposals.reason: Matches 太尉 and 李存審; Grand Preceptor and Li Cun'an are incorrect.

proposals.before: On the sixth day of the second month in the fourth year Zhao Zaili rebelled at Ye; Cunxu sent Yuan Xingqin against him;
proposals.after: On the sixth day of the second month in the fourth year Zhao Zaili rebelled at Weizhou; Cunxu sent Yuan Xingqin against him;
proposals.reason: Chinese 據魏州反 is Weizhou, not Ye (鄴), which appears only later.

proposals.before: Fourth year, second month, sixth day: Zhao Zaili held Ye prefecture in revolt; Zhuangzong sent Yuan Xingqin to lead troops against him;
proposals.after: Fourth year, second month, sixth day: Zhao Zaili held Weizhou in revolt; Zhuangzong sent Yuan Xingqin to lead troops against him;
proposals.reason: 魏州 is Weizhou, not Ye prefecture.

proposals.before: Xingqin was unfavorable and withdrew to guard Weizhou.
proposals.after: Xingqin met with reverse and withdrew to guard Weizhou.
proposals.reason: 不利 means the campaign went badly, not that Xingqin was morally unfavorable.

proposals.before: Siyuan shouted and rebuked their treason; they answered, "Yesterday at Beizhou garrison you showed no mercy;
proposals.after: Siyuan shouted and rebuked their treason; they answered, "Yesterday at the Beizhou garrison the sovereign showed no generous pardon;
proposals.reason: 主上 is the reigning sovereign (Zhuangzong), not Siyuan, whom the mutineers address as 令公.

proposals.before: We have agreed with the garrison to drive off the other columns; we want you emperor south of the river and our lord emperor north."
proposals.after: We have agreed with the garrison to drive off the other columns; we want the sovereign emperor south of the river and you, our lord, emperor north."
proposals.reason: 欲主上帝河南，請令公帝河北 contrasts 主上 (Zhuangzong) with 令公 (Siyuan).

proposals.before: Siyuan wept and refused; they shouted, "If you will not go north, where will you go?
proposals.after: Siyuan wept and refused; they shouted, "Where does our lord mean to go?
proposals.reason: 令公欲何之 asks where he will go; the idiomatic line invents a refused northern journey.

proposals.before: Xingqin held Weizhou and slandered him by memorial; Siyuan answered; Cunxu sent his son Congshen and the eunuch Bai Congxun with an edict.
proposals.after: Xingqin held Weizhou and slandered him by memorial; Siyuan answered; Cunxu sent the Emperor's son Congshen and the eunuch Bai Congxun with an edict.
proposals.reason: 帝子從審 is Siyuan's son (帝 in this annals), not Cunxu's son; 莊宗遣 marks Zhuangzong as sender only.

proposals.before: At dawn Zhu Shouyin sent word, "Luoyang is burning and looting will not stop—come quickly."
proposals.after: At dawn Zhu Shouyin sent word, "The capital is in great disorder; burning and looting will not stop—come quickly."
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English invents Luoyang; the Chinese names only the capital 京城.

proposals.before: Jiji's Shu campaign had not returned; Siyuan told Zhu Shouyin, "Patrol well and await the Prince of Wei.
proposals.after: At that time Prince of Wei Jiji's campaign against Shu had not yet returned; the Emperor told Zhu Shouyin, "Kindly patrol and soothe, and await the Prince of Wei."
proposals.reason: The courtesy 公善巡撫 is an imperative, not a claim of skill; 征蜀 is a campaign against Shu; 帝 is the Emperor.

proposals.before: (The 《Miscellaneous Dreams of the Northern Realm》 records: Zhuangzong's younger brothers Cunji and Cunque hid in a south-mountain peasant household; someone reported this to An Chonghui, and Chonghui said, "The lord below has issued an edict to seek them; the Emperor's benevolence will surely not harm them—better secretly order them killed."
proposals.after: (The 《Miscellaneous Dreams of the Northern Realm》 records: Zhuangzong's younger brothers Cunji and Cunque hid in a south-mountain peasant household; someone reported this to An Chonghui, and Chonghui said, "The ruler has issued an edict to seek them; the Emperor's benevolence will surely not harm them—better secretly order them killed."
proposals.reason: 主上以下詔 means the ruler issued an edict, not a lord who is below.

proposals.before: He thus made the living smear themselves with ashes and soldiers hunger in cold, making a sore upon All-under-Heaven and exhausting human weariness to the limit.
proposals.after: He thus drove the living into utter misery and soldiers into hunger and cold, making a sore upon All-under-Heaven and exhausting human weariness to the limit.
proposals.reason: 生靈塗炭 is the idiom of people plunged into misery, not a literal smearing with ashes.

proposals.before: Summer and autumn field taxes may add nothing beyond the original grain levy per dou and ground-head money.
proposals.after: Summer and autumn field taxes may add nothing beyond the original grain levy in shi and dou and ground-head money.
proposals.reason: Chinese 石鬥 is a corruption of 石斗, the paired volume measures shi and dou, not a levy counted only per dou.

proposals.before: Summer and autumn field taxes, apart from the originally levied grain per dou and the ground-head money, may have no further surcharges.
proposals.after: Summer and autumn field taxes, apart from the originally levied grain in shi and dou and the ground-head money, may have no further surcharges.
proposals.reason: Chinese 石鬥 is a corruption of 石斗; the original levy is stated in shi and dou, not only per dou.
